title: Start the API and inspect routing

contentBlocks.body:
**Objective.** Start the real ASP.NET Core host and observe routing before adding a domain endpoint.

This is a real project lab in projects/inventory-desk, also available from the Projects page as a source download. Work in an isolated copy of the reference project so you can compare your change with a known baseline. Read InventoryDesk.Api/Program.cs; InventoryDesk.Api/InventoryDesk.Api.csproj before editing. Trace one request from the UI or test through the boundary that owns the behavior.

contentBlocks.code:
dotnet run --project InventoryDesk.Api
# In a second terminal:
curl http://127.0.0.1:5080/health/live

contentBlocks.body:
**Acceptance criteria.** The host listens on loopback, /health/live returns 200 JSON, and an unknown API route is distinguishable from a valid response.

**Make a meaningful variation.** Add a read-only /api/version route with an explicit response DTO and an HTTP test. Write the observable expectation before editing the implementation. If the variation exposes a defect, keep the smallest failing fixture as a regression test.
Review rubric: The final image runs as a nonroot user, runtime data is outside the image, and a successful process start is not confused with readiness.

**Explain the boundary.** Which layer decides the response status and route contract? Describe both a successful case and a rejected or missing-data case. Compare actual output with the acceptance criteria, including status codes, persisted values, and user-visible feedback where relevant.

**Evidence to keep.** Save the focused test result, a short before/after diff, and a note explaining one tradeoff. Completing the quiz records this lesson's concepts; it does not run the companion checks or certify that the project milestone is finished.
